Hey guys and gals! Today, I proudly present Voatify - an app for Voat that's available now on the App Store!

Quick App Info

This app is the first version, very basic, and just read-only. That means you can only view submissions/comments (and you cannot yet log in, upvote, comment, etc. - but these features are coming soon)

The app is FREE, but it comes with small a non-intrusive banner ad at the bottom of subverse screens. I basically quit my developer day-job to work on this full time as well as other potential iOS projects that I have been sitting on. I understand that ads are still annoying, so I made it as unintrusive as possible while giving an easy way for the community to support me if they like it. If either this endeavor or my next project can be sustainable, then I'll be able to continue to work on this full time to make it the best Voat app for iOS.

If you guys get a chance to try it out, let me know how it is! Either drop a comment here, or make a post over at /v/voatify and tell me what's good (or not)! If you have more time and want to look at some more walls of text, read on!

Who am I and how I came to Voat

Like many of you, I am a user who migrated from one of the great exoduses of Reddit. I had never been a very political person, and for some reason I started following the US elections a few months ago out of sheer curiosity. Then I started noticing strange things, like /r/politics slowly removing wikileaks articles in favor of Trump bashing. Before long, I noticed myself going solely to /r/the_donald to actually follow real news and wikileaks developments. During that time, they moved all of the podesta stuff to the pizzagate subreddit. And then soon after the election, the pizzagate subreddit was banned. And then was about the 2nd or 3rd time that Voat was mentioned to me, so I decided to check out. I saw that the pizzagate investigations did indeed migrate to Voat, so I came, created an account, and went to the App Store to download an app. Well, to my (unfortunate) surprise, there really wasn't one. There was one obscure app that came up that cost 99 cents and had bad ratings that said it was broken, so that was a no go.

But then I remembered...I'm actually an iOS developer! I can just make an app for myself! So after deliberating for a few weeks, I started development the day after Thanksgiving. During this time, I also started to get to know the Voat community. And the next few weeks, what I witnessed was amazing. Although some of the comments seemed crazy and outrageous to me as a former Reddit user, it was refreshing to see people be completely honest. And users were not getting banned for it! But then I witnessed the 2 attempted takeovers and saw how the community as well as one of the owners handled it. That really solidified it for me in the necessity of a community/organization like Voat.

I want to thank @PuttItOut and @Atko for creating this community of free speech. I have to say, it feels really good knowing that I was given skills to contribute to such an endeavor. I hope you guys like the app. Please give me plenty of feedback over at /v/voatify - what you like, don't like, and what you want. Thanks for reading. Hope you like it.

P.S. - Please give Voatify a super duper good rating on the App Store if you like it. Thanks, that is all.
